- Constant-reply and copy strategies on pattern, coding and knowledge exact items.
- Token-length balance of the 200 grammar pairs: a length-only model scores -1.5, so it is balanced.
- Leak of bare bench questions into fact, chat and instruction training text: 0/251.
- Generation budgets against answer and reference lengths.
- I eyeballed all 200 frozen grammar pairs and 60 instruction items, and spot-checked the KB for contested capitals, transcontinental countries and animal class/legs facts. It looked careful.

Not covered or not verifiable here:
- The real tok-v1. The token findings use a probe tokenizer trained on generated text, so token counts are approximate; the boundary finding relies only on the pre-tokenizer regex plus merging, which holds for any tokenizer trained on the code share.
- A trained model's actual generations: there is no GPU and no corpora.
- Whether real mbpp rows contain a reserved bench def line (needs network).
- Windows-specific C-stack behaviour of ast.parse on the hostile 20 KB tests. These are CPython-guarded, and any error maps to a fixed string.

I did not re-report deferred or ruled items: format-only checkers and the instruction floor, compare mention counts, the word_problem 'within 5' tell, the contains_any over-acceptance, the TimeLimit wall-clock net and near-paraphrase templates.

findings.evidence: Probe: trained a 4096-vocab byte-level BPE with train_tokenizer on generator text (6000 code docs plus facts, reasoning, patterns and fixture prose; scratchpad tokprobe.py). The bench prompt tail is ['."""', 'Ċ']; prompt plus reference gives ['."""', 'ĊĠĠĠ', 'Ġreturn', ...]. For 50/50 function items, the prompt tokens are not a prefix of the prompt+reference tokens. The same alignment check over every other non-chat bench item (reasoning 700 options, pattern 150, knowledge 650, consistency 480, coding outputs 100) found 0 mismatches. In code training text, the token after a bare 'Ċ' was a pure-space token 0 times out of 21,941 (top: print 8999, Output 3001, Ċ 2999, for, def, if). A closing docstring was followed by 'ĊĠĠĠ' 2011/2011 times. I checked the ledger, ADR 0001 and the Task 12/16 reports: there is no ruling on this. The Task 16 fakes are keyed by exact token tuples, so they cannot show it.
findings.fix: Show the model the header without its trailing newline: the item prompt ends at the closing `"""`, so the first generated token is the 'ĊĠĠĠ' it was trained on. Keep check_args['prompt'] (with the newline) for building the MiniPy source; function_body already skips the empty first line of a reply that starts with '\n'. Start the reference with '\n'. Add a test with a trained fixture tokenizer: for every non-chat bench item, tok.encode(prompt) must be a token prefix of tok.encode(prompt + continuation). This must be fixed before bench-v1 freezes.
findings.line: 878 (_Variant.prompt ends with '"""\n'), 1004-1009 (item prompt and check_args prompt), 927 (training text = prompt + body); see also evals/suite.py:151-154 and tokenizer.py:80
findings.scenario:
tok-v1 uses a ByteLevel pre-tokenizer with the GPT-2 regex (tokenizer.py:80). Its `\s+(?!\S)` rule splits the training text `..."""
    return x * 2` into '."""', '
   ' (newline plus 3 spaces), ' return'. BPE merges that first piece into one token (ĊĠĠĠ) because code makes up 1/8 of the tokenizer sample. The bench prompt `def f(x):
    """doc"""
` ends at the end of the string, so its last token is a bare 'Ċ'. suite._prompt_ids feeds encode_doc(prompt) unchanged, with no token healing. In the code training text, a bare 'Ċ' is always followed by a column-0 statement ('print', 'Output', 'def', 'for', 'Ċ') and never by a space token. A closing docstring is always followed by 'ĊĠĠĠ'. So a model that has learned to write bodies still continues at column 0 with greedy decoding, for example `print(add(2, 3))  # 5`. checkers.function_body (checkers.py:152-162) cuts at that first unindented line and returns ''. The source is then the bare def plus docstring, which returns None, so every hidden test fails. This hits all 50 fmt:function items, a third of coding, so the coding category can never go much above about 67% raw, and the 'coding/fam:*' function tags stay near 0 in the frozen bench-v1 whatever the player trains.
findings.title: Function-completion prompts end on a lone newline token that training never puts before a function body, so all 50 function items are effectively impossible to pass

findings.evidence: Probe (scratchpad prior_probe.py / cons_probe.py) on the frozen streams skill_rng('knowledge'/'consistency', 'bench'). The subject-blind 'most frequent object of the relation' picker scored: animal_legs 11/16, animal_class 9/16, baby_animal 7/15, vehicle_travel 7/15, shape_sides 4/10. Category score via evals.scoring.normalize: 18.8. The ledger rules only on option-text priors for consistency (Task 16) and on answer ranks for reasoning (Task 11); nothing covers the knowledge answer distribution.
findings.fix: In the bench sampler (knowledge and consistency), stratify by answer. Within each relation, draw the object uniformly (or cap each object at about 1/N_OPTIONS of the relation's items), then a subject with that object. With uniform distractors, the 4-option set is then exchangeable and any subject-blind rule gets exactly 1/4. Add a test that the 'most frequent object' picker stays within about chance + 0.05 on knowledge and consistency. Regenerate before bench-v1 freezes.
findings.line: 46-55 (_sample_facts: uniform over facts within a relation), 68-79 (_bench_pools), 144-164 (knowledge_bench_items), 175 (consistency_groups); kb.py:161-178 (distractors uniform over the other objects)
findings.scenario: Bench facts are drawn uniformly within each relation, so the true answer follows the KB's skewed object counts. The bench pools have mammal at 41% of animal_class, four at 45% of animal_legs, four at 50% of shape_sides, by water at 38% of vehicle_travel and calf at 31% of baby_animal. Distractors are drawn uniformly from the other objects. A model that never learned a single subject fact but picks whichever option is that relation's most common object gets 55/150 MC items (0.367 against chance 0.25) and 5/50 exact items ('four'). With the suite's chance (mean 0.1875 over the 200 items), its knowledge score normalizes to 18.8/100. Over 30 other bench draws the MC rate averages 0.40 (0.35-0.47), so this is systematic, not this seed. An early LM picks up exactly this prior ('...legs does a koala have? Answer: four'), so knowledge reads well above 0 before any fact is known. That breaks R5's 'score 0 at chance' and misleads G3 and the players. consistency_groups uses the same sampler. Its frozen draw happens to sit at chance (0.25), but its expected value is 0.29.
findings.title: Knowledge multiple choice is gameable by each relation's most common answer: a model that ignores the subject scores about 19/100

findings.evidence: The probe tokenizer above splits it into 9 tokens ['ĠB','and','ar','ĠSer','i','ĠB','eg','aw','an']. Every other exact answer is 4 tokens or fewer. The real tok-v1 is trained on more prose and may need 7-9, so this is borderline and unverified without the real tokenizer.
findings.fix: Give knowledge exact items headroom, for example max_new_tokens = max(8, 4 + longest answer length in characters // 2). Or add a build-time check, once tok-v1 exists, that every exact answer fits its budget.
findings.scenario: The frozen knowledge bench has the exact item 'Question: Fill in the blank. The capital city of Brunei is called ___.\nAnswer:' with the only answer 'Bandar Seri Begawan'. Generation stops after 8 tokens, and extract='first_line' then compares the truncated text, for example 'Bandar Seri Begaw'. If tok-v1 needs 9 or more tokens for ' Bandar Seri Begawan', no model can ever pass this item.
findings.title: The knowledge free-answer budget of 8 new tokens may be too short for 'Bandar Seri Begawan', a frozen bench answer

findings.evidence: I read suite.py, types.py, pyproject.toml and grepped every test in scope plus test_bench.py for a golden digest or snapshot of bench items: there is none. Every ledger entry says bench-v1 freezes once players use it.
findings.fix: Add a test that hashes a canonical JSON of build_suite().items (prompts, options, answers, check_args and tags in order) against a recorded digest, with a message that any intended change must bump SUITE_VERSION. Optionally store the digest in the bench report.
findings.scenario: bench-v1 is regenerated in-process from the generator code, the kb_data JSON and numpy Generator streams (choice, permutation, integers). Several things would quietly produce different items still labelled 'bench-v1': a later edit to kb_data (a fact fix in M3), a word added to a generator table, or a numpy upgrade that changes a Generator algorithm (numpy is >=2.5 with no upper bound, and NEP 19 does not promise stream compatibility for Generator). Spec §4.7 keys leaderboards on (bench version, category), so scores from before and after such a change would be silently incomparable. The gate's code digest notices the change for caching, but no test or check ties the label to the content.
findings.title: Nothing pins the bench-v1 item set, so it can change silently under the same version label

find:skills/integration.coverage_note: Read in full: minipy/interpreter.py and __init__.py; skills/types.py, checkers.py, code.py, facts.py, kb.py, reasoning.py, patterns.py, instructions.py, grammar.py and __init__.py. Also read the cross-task consumers: evals/suite.py, evals/scoring.py, tokenizer.py, the gate's false-fact probes, G3 and prefix trimming (gate.py), runs.py's source digests, airace_content assemble.py (recipes, GENERATORS, prepare_content, topic check), build.py (tokenizer sample, false-fact plan), and the normalize_text contract. Read the ledger, deferred minors, global constraints, ADR 0001 and plan Task 12. Ran the 4 in-scope test files: 433 passed in 36 s. Probes, all scripts and outputs under the scratchpad: (a) trained a tok-v1-like 4096 BPE on generated plus prose text, then checked every bench prompt for trailing whitespace and token-prefix consistency, and the reply budgets of every Exact and Check item; (b) trained a tiny LM on code_train_docs and ran the real function items both ways (0/50 vs 50/50); (c) checked bench-v1, every training generator and the false-fact plan for PYTHONHASHSEED independence (identical digests for seeds 0, 1 and 12345); (d) timed every generator and extrapolated to full-scale token targets (each well under 1 minute); (e) confirmed generated programs never reach MiniPy's 256-step wall-clock read (max 207 steps over 20,400 programs), so the corpus build is deterministic; (f) generator topics vs data.corpus.TOPICS, KB train_templates[0] subject-before-object order (all OK), and UTF-8/ASCII KB I/O; (g) MiniPy callers (only code.py and checkers.py) and their error handling; (h) a dead-code scan of the scope (none found). One accident: my first probe wrote tok_probe.json into ml/ through a relative path. I moved it to the scratchpad straight away, git status is clean, and nothing in the repo, its index or HEAD was changed. Not covered: real Hugging Face text (no network), so my tokenizer is an approximation. The Critical finding does not depend on it: its token behaviour comes from code text only and is confirmed by the trained model. The reply-budget finding does depend on it. GPU/CUDA runs and Windows execution were not possible here; nothing in this scope is platform-specific beyond the deterministic numpy and blake2b streams. Not re-reported, because the ledger rules on them: form-only checkers, partition design, consistency and instruction-floor rules, MiniPy limits, and the deferred minors.

findings.evidence:
1) Trained a 4096 BPE in the scratchpad on a tok-v1-like equal-share sample: 1.76 MB of code_train_docs, 2.5 MB reasoning+patterns, 2.5 MB fact prose, 1 MB chats, 11 MB prose. Results: 'Ċ' is the prompt's last token, while training has '."""' -> 'ĊĠĠĠ' -> 'Ġreturn'. The token after a closing '"""' was 'ĊĠĠĠ' in 7001/7001 cases. Tokens after a bare 'Ċ' started with a space 0/51,265 times, and started with 'ĊĠ' 0 times. 2) Trained a ModelShape(2,128,128) model for 7 CPU minutes on 2.9M tokens of code_train_docs and ran the real 50 bench function items through TorchLM greedy generation and CHECKERS. As written: 0/50 pass, 0/50 replies start an indented body (replies are 'print(add_numbers(15, 18))  # 31', 'print(dbl(0))  # 0'). Same model with the prompt ending at the closing quotes: 50/50 pass (replies '
    return n + m

print(...)'). 3) Searched the ledger, handoff and task reports: the boundary was never discussed. The reply-budget test (test_bench.py:707-739) measures reference length only and cannot catch this.
findings.fix: Give the model the header up to the closing quotes, with no trailing newline: in _bench_functions use CheckItem(..., prompt=v.prompt.rstrip('\n'), check_args={'prompt': v.prompt, ...}). check_args['prompt'] keeps its newline, so the reference and the plan test still pass. A reply starting with '\n' already works, because function_body keeps a leading empty line and Python accepts the blank line. Leave _Variant.prompt unchanged so the training partition (code.py:911) and the corpus stay as they are; no rebuild is needed, and the change alters MEASURING_SOURCES, so gate caches refresh by themselves. Add a regression test: no non-chat bench prompt ends in whitespace, or, better, encode(prompt) is a token prefix of encode(prompt + reference/answer) under a BPE trained with the build's pre-tokenizer. Record the deviation from plan line 1176 in ADR 0001, because bench-v1 has not frozen yet.
findings.line: 878 (_Variant.prompt ends with '"""\n'), 1004-1009 (CheckItem.prompt = v.prompt); consumed at ml/src/airace_ml/evals/suite.py:151-154 (encode_doc(prompt)) and :205-210; format mandated by plan line 1176
findings.scenario: The tokenizer is byte-level BPE with the GPT-2 pre-tokenizer (tokenizer.py:80). In training text the newline after a docstring merges with the body's indentation into one pre-token ('\n   ' + ' return'), which the BPE learns as the single token 'ĊĠĠĠ'. The bench prompt ends exactly at that newline, so its last token is a bare 'Ċ'. In all generated code training text, a bare 'Ċ' is never followed by indentation: it is always followed by a column-0 line ('print', 'Output', 'def', ...). So given the bench prompt, a trained model writes the usage line 'print(name(...))  # ...'. function_body() then cuts the reply at that first unindented line and returns ''. Every hidden test fails, and every model reads 0 on all 50 'fmt:function' items. Consequences: coding is capped at about 67, every function-family tag reads 0 for discoveries, and bench-v1 would freeze with this. The gate's G3 needs the code-heavy mix to lead coding by 2 seed-spreads. With half of coding dead, that rests on the output-prediction items alone, so G3 can fail for a reason unrelated to feasibility. Probe tokenizer evidence: 50/50 function items have prompt tokens that are not a prefix of prompt+reference. All other bench prompts are consistent (0 mismatches over 770 plain items), and gate.py trims its own prefixes of trailing whitespace (gate.py:739-743).
findings.title: Function-completion prompts end on a bare newline token that training never follows with indentation, so no trained model can pass the 50 function items (a third of coding in bench-v1)

findings.evidence: Built the bench-v1 suite and measured every knowledge exact answer under the probe tokenizer described above. 'Bandar Seri Begawan' is 10 tokens, 'Santo Domingo' 7, everything else 5 or fewer. The probe is weaker on English than the real tok-v1 will be (' Wednesday' came out as 4 tokens), so this is an upper estimate. Hence low-to-medium confidence.
findings.fix: Before bench-v1 freezes, give knowledge ExactItems a roomier fixed budget (for example max_new_tokens=12; patterns and coding keep theirs). Alternatively, re-run the real-tokenizer budget test as part of the Task 15 build checklist and adjust before the gate.
findings.line: 164 (ExactItem(...) with default max_new_tokens=8 from types.py:116); item knowledge-0168
findings.scenario: A reply needs the leading space plus every answer token within max_new_tokens=8. The probe tokenizer splits ' Bandar Seri Begawan' into 10 tokens: ĠB/and/ar/ĠS/er/i/ĠB/eg/aw/an. A real tok-v1 with better English merges probably gives 7-9. If it gives 9 or more, no model can answer knowledge-0168 in full, and the guard test test_every_answer_fits_its_reply_budget_with_the_real_tokenizer (tests/test_bench.py:737-739) will fail on the owner's PC right after the full corpus build. The owner is not technical and cannot act on that failure. bench-v1 would then need a change after its data and tokenizer exist.
findings.title: Knowledge exact items keep the default 8-token reply budget, but bench-v1 asks for 'Bandar Seri Begawan', which a 4096-entry BPE likely splits into 8 or more tokens

find:skills/robustness.coverage_note:
I read in full: minipy/interpreter.py; skills/types.py, kb.py, facts.py, reasoning.py, patterns.py, code.py, instructions.py, grammar.py and checkers.py. I also read the relevant callers: evals/suite.py (prompt encoding), evals/scoring.py (exact_match/extract), content/assemble.py (full-scale generator use), textproc.normalize_text, experiments/runs.source_digest, and the tokenizer.

Ran: the 4 scoped test files, 433 passed in about 37 s; the slowest test is 6 s.

Probes, all under the scratchpad:
- MiniPy: about 70 hostile or edge programs. These covered deep or pathological parse within the 20k cap (unary, not, call, index, plus and lambda chains), CR/CRLF/BOM/NUL/surrogates, huge int literals, cyclic and aliased lists, Unicode upper(), int() of Unicode digits, global +=, every unsupported node kind, and recursion. There were no host exceptions; the worst case took 23 ms.
- Determinism: bench-v1 hashes the same under two PYTHONHASHSEEDs. No salted hash(), wall-clock randomness or set-order dependence was found; sets are used only for membership.
- CPython vs MiniPy: our own generated programs, run under python -I, print identically for all 100 bench output programs, 10,024 training programs, every function-doc usage comment and every function reference against its tests.
- Checkers: 30 degenerate replies (empty, special-token text, repetition, emoji, 5000 chars, infinite-loop bodies) against all 170 bench CheckItems. There were no exceptions and every reference passes.
- Full-scale extrapolation: each generator needs at most about 35 s at the full-scale doc counts (about 30k-220k docs); generated docs are 99-100% distinct.
- KB: no falsifiable fact lacks a wrong object, the KB is ASCII-only, and Turkey/turkey and Mercury/mercury are distinct subjects.
- Token budgets and prompt boundaries for every plain-prompt bench item, measured with a self-trained 4096 BPE.
- Windows: .gitattributes forces eol=lf. All scoped text I/O passes encoding='utf-8'. There is no multiprocessing, and the skills modules do no path handling. uv.lock numpy 2.5.3 matches the cloud venv. Git history shows the Task 9 MiniPy tests, including the 20 KB deep-nesting cases, were committed from the owner's Windows machine (+0200); Task 12 code has only run on Linux but uses no OS facilities.

Not covered: the real tok-v1, which does not exist here, so findings 1 and 3 were measured with an approximating tokenizer (finding 1 holds for any BPE that merges newline+space, which a sample of 12.5% code will do). Not executed on Windows or CUDA. Earlier rulings and deferred minors were not re-raised: TimeLimit is wall-clock but unreachable at 10k steps; form-only checkers; the residual `**` and .count failures; the near-paraphrase leaks.

findings.evidence: I trained a 4096-vocab BPE with train_tokenizer() on generated code/reasoning/pattern/fact/instruction docs plus the fixtures. Build-time tok-v1 uses an equal share per dataset (build.py:200-218), so code is about 12.5% of its sample and the same merges are expected. Results: the prompt tail tokens are ['Ġanswer', '."""', 'Ċ']. Joint prompt+reference encoding gives ['."""', 'ĊĠĠĠ', 'Ġreturn', ...]. encode(prompt)+encode(reference) == encode(prompt+reference) for 0/50 function items. In 3000 training code docs, `Ċ` followed by a space-led token occurs 0 times, against 6163 merged newline+space tokens. The token after a docstring close is `ĊĠĠĠ` 1990 times. After a lone `Ċ` the next token is print 5990, Output 2010, Ċ 1990, for 399, def 341, if 330. The same separate-vs-joint check over every other plain-prompt bench item (reasoning 700, pattern 150, knowledge 650, consistency 480 continuations, the 100 output-prediction items) found 0 mismatches. Only function items are affected.
findings.fix:
End function prompts at the closing `"""` (drop the trailing "
"). Make the reference "
" + body. function_body() already keeps a leading empty line, so source = prompt + function_body(reply) then reads `..."""
    return ...`. Training docs stay unchanged. Add a regression test with a BPE trained on code_train_docs: for every non-chat bench item, encode(prompt)+encode(continuation) == encode(prompt+continuation). This changes bench-v1 content, so do it before the owner's first real gate run.
findings.line: 878 (prompt property), 1004-1012 (CheckItem built from v.prompt); consumed by ml/src/airace_ml/evals/suite.py:151-154 (_prompt_ids -> encode_doc) and ml/src/airace_ml/skills/checkers.py:183
findings.scenario:
The function prompt is `def f(a, b):
    """doc"""
`. The ByteLevel/GPT-2 pre-tokenizer splits the final "
" off as a lone `Ċ` token. In every training document (code.py:927, `variant.prompt + variant.body(...)`) the same newline is followed by indentation, and the tokenizer always merges the two into a newline+spaces token such as `ĊĠĠĠ`. So the model never sees `Ċ` followed by an indented line. After a lone `Ċ` it has only seen column-0 tokens (`print`, `Output`, `def`, `for`, `if`). Greedy decoding therefore continues with a top-level line. function_body() cuts at that line, the body is empty, and the item fails. Every model will score about 0 on these 50 items (one third of the coding category) whatever it has learned. This is a silent measurement error in bench-v1 that also weakens G3 (code mix should lead coding). Note the plan itself mandated this prompt format (plan Task 12 interfaces), so the implementation is faithful to the plan.
findings.title: Function-completion bench prompts end in a lone newline token that never appears before an indented line in training, so all 50 function items are effectively unanswerable

findings.evidence: build_suite() is deterministic today. I serialized it to canonical JSON and got the same sha256 (5c47335940e0c3ac…) under PYTHONHASHSEED=0 and 987654. grep over tests/test_bench.py and the four scoped test files found no digest, golden file or pinned item content. Only ids and counts are asserted (test_code_instr_grammar.py:384, 764).
findings.fix: Add a test that hashes canonical JSON of build_suite().items (asdict per item, sort_keys) and compares it to a pinned digest. Comment that a mismatch means either restoring the old behaviour or bumping SUITE_VERSION. Pin it only after the function-prompt fix lands.
findings.line: 87, 116-128 (SUITE_VERSION and _bench_items built from the skills generators); generators in ml/src/airace_ml/skills/*.py and kb_data/*.json
findings.scenario: The spec says leaderboards key on (bench version, category) and the rulings treat bench-v1 as frozen. In fact the suite is rebuilt in every process from the generators, the KB JSON, MiniPy (code.py:477-480 accepts programs by running them) and checkers (instructions.py:267 selects worlds with CHECKERS['one_word']). Any later edit can change bench-v1 items under the same name. Examples: a KB typo fix, a checker tweak, a MiniPy change, the code.py fix above, or a numpy bump in uv.lock that alters Generator.choice/permutation streams (NumPy does not promise stream stability across versions). No test notices. The gate's measuring-source digest only triggers re-measurement; it does not force a version bump. Scores labelled bench-v1 from different builds would then compare different tests.
findings.title: bench-v1 is regenerated from code at runtime with no pinned content digest, so it can drift silently under the same suite version

findings.evidence: With a 4096 BPE trained on generated corpora that contain this fact plus the fixtures, ' Bandar Seri Begawan' -> ['ĠB','and','ar','ĠS','er','i','ĠBeg','a','wan'] = 9 tokens > 8. Every other ExactItem fit its budget: pattern max 3/8, knowledge next longest 'Santo Domingo' 4/8, coding output and instruction references within 16/64. Real tok-v1 merges are unknown here, hence medium confidence.
findings.fix: Size max_new_tokens per item from the longest accepted answer (for example max(8, 4 + len(answer)//2)). Or keep exact items to answers that fit comfortably and leave long names to multiple choice.
findings.scenario: knowledge-0168 ('The capital city of Brunei is called ___.') accepts only 'Bandar Seri Begawan'. Free-answer knowledge items get the default 8 new tokens. Under a 4096-vocab byte-level BPE the answer plus its leading space takes about 9 tokens. Generation stops before the answer is complete, the extracted line never matches, and the item is wrong for every model. It is a small but permanent deflation of the knowledge score in a bench that is meant to be frozen.
findings.title: Knowledge exact item 'Bandar Seri Begawan' likely needs more tokens than the 8-token generation budget

findings.evidence: Read gate.py speed/legibility/growth/forgetting/preparation (lines 990-1200): each takes `seed = self.seeds[0]` or reuses the seed-1 starter run, and only lines 1061 and 1089 iterate `self.seeds`. Checked the ledger (progress.md Task 20 rulings, task-20-dispatch-notes.md rulings 1-14) and ADR 0001: none rules on the seed count. eval_forgetting/eval_prep (gate.py:458-560) take single numbers, not per-seed lists.
findings.fix: Run G6 and G7 (and preferably G2 and G5) for every seed. Evaluate on the seed means, and require the margin to beat the seed spread as G3 does (for example drop and recovery on means, with a spread check). If the GPU budget does not allow that, record a ruling and amend spec §4.12 to say which criteria are single-seed and why.
findings.scenario: The owner runs `airace-ml gate --out runs/gate-1` with the default seeds 1,2,3. Only differentiation (gate.py:1061) and seed variation (gate.py:1089) loop over the seeds. Every other experiment uses `self.seeds[0]` only. G6 then passes or fails on one story model and one pair of code-only children (drop >= 3 points, recovery >= 50%). G7 passes or fails on one light/thorough pair and one unchecked/checked pair (ratio <= 0.8). Training-seed spread on creativity/language scores and on garble/false-fact rates is unmeasured, so a single seed can produce a FAIL that starts a step-8 iteration chasing noise, or a PASS that M2 is then built on. G2 also rests on one starter model. The spec says "Measured by an automated experiment suite (3 seeds each)". The plan's Task 20 table (plan:1868-1873) narrows this to "seed 1", and no ledger ruling, ADR or spec amendment records that narrowing.
findings.title: Feasibility gate runs 3 seeds only for G3/G4; G1, G2, G5, G6 and G7 each decide on a single seed, against spec §4.12's "3 seeds each"

findings.evidence: Read pyproject.toml (content extra), CLAUDE.md:30-39, sources.py:82-93, the content cli.py error path and plan:1478. Checked with `uv run --help` that extras are opt-in (`--extra`) and that `--exact` is off for `uv run`.
findings.fix: Change the CLAUDE.md build line to `cd ml && python -m uv sync --extra content && python -m uv run airace-content build --scale {tiny,full}`. Note that a plain `uv sync` removes the extra. Make the DatasetsUnavailable message say `python -m uv sync --extra content`. Add the `python -m uv run pytest -m gpu` line.
findings.scenario: On Windows the owner (or the local session following CLAUDE.md) runs `cd ml && python -m uv sync`, then `python -m uv run airace-content build --scale full`. `datasets` is an optional extra (pyproject `[project.optional-dependencies] content`), and neither `uv sync` nor `uv run` installs extras without `--extra content`. So hf_fetch raises DatasetsUnavailable and the CLI exits 1 with "install the content extra (uv sync --extra content)". That remedy cannot run as typed on the owner's PC, where uv is not on PATH. After a later `python -m uv sync` (the documented setup command, an exact sync), `datasets` is removed again. The plan's Task 15 step 2 has the right command (`uv sync --extra content && uv run airace-content build --scale full`), but CLAUDE.md, the doc a resuming session reads first, does not. CLAUDE.md also lists no GPU-test command (`pytest -m gpu`, needed for test_starter_speed_gpu and the CUDA bf16 tests on the owner's machine).
findings.title: CLAUDE.md's corpus-build command omits the `content` extra, so the owner's next step (full build) fails at once, and the error's own fix uses bare `uv`

findings.evidence: Ran build_suite() and counted tag prefixes per category: language/reasoning/pattern {'fam'} only; knowledge/consistency {'topic','rel'}; coding {'fam','fmt'}; instruction {'topic','fam'}. Every category is missing at least two of topic/skill/fmt. Grepped the ledger and ADR: no ruling on the tag scheme.
findings.fix: Before bench-v1 freezes, give every item a topic:, skill: and fmt: tag (for example skill = family/relation, fmt = mc/pair/exact/check/story, topic = the generator's topic or 'other'). Tags are not item text, so scores do not change. Otherwise record a ruling that defers the full tag space to M4.
findings.line: 820 (also reasoning.py:451, patterns.py:198, code.py:981/1013, instructions.py:614, facts knowledge/consistency items, evals/creativity.py:136)
findings.scenario: Spec §4.7: "Every category stores per-item results tagged by topic x skill x format; those tags feed discoveries" (also §4.9). The real bench-v1 tags are as follows. Language, reasoning and pattern items have only `fam:` (no topic, no format). Knowledge and consistency have `rel:`+`topic:` (no format). Coding has `fam:`+`fmt:` (no topic). Instruction has `fam:`+`topic:`. Creativity has `fmt:`+`topic:`. No item has all three axes, and no `skill:` axis exists anywhere. The discovery engine (M4) and any BenchReport stored by the M2 registry therefore lack the combinatorial space the spec describes. The plan narrowed tags to `fam:<name>` without a recorded ruling.
findings.title: Benchmark items are not tagged topic x skill x format as spec §4.7 requires; most categories carry a single axis

findings.evidence: Read trainer._evaluate and events.py (event types: Progress, HeldoutEval, Sample, Instability, Done). Grepped the repo for 'mini-eval': only the spec line. The plan's Task 8 telemetry bullet (plan:902) has no mini-eval.
findings.fix: Record a deferral to M2 in the ledger or spec. Or add an optional mini-eval at eval steps, e.g. run_benchmarks(max_items_per_category≈10, no creativity) emitted as a new event.
findings.scenario: Spec §4.7 (spec:167) requires a mini-eval during training for live charts. The trainer's periodic `_evaluate` emits only HeldoutEval losses and probe-prompt Samples. No benchmark items are run during training, and no event type or hook exists for one. The plan's Task 8 telemetry list omits it, and neither the ledger nor an ADR defers it to M2. M2's live-training view will find no M1 support for this spec item.
findings.title: Spec §4.7 "tiny mini-eval runs during training for live charts" has no implementation and no recorded deferral

findings.evidence: Probe on a tiny corpus built from the fixtures (scratchpad): A completed with last_mixture {'creative': 0.667, 'notebook': 0.333}. B raised `MixtureError dataset 'notebook' has weight but no usable documents`. test_replay_notebook_and_coaching only covers a parent without custom datasets.
findings.fix: Either drop custom datasets from the replayed parent mixture when the child supplies none (renormalising the rest), or name the cause in the error ("the replayed mix includes your notebook; include notebook entries or lower replay"). Record the M2 contract that the server always re-sends notebook and coaching for replay.
findings.scenario: Spec §4.5 "Review what it knows = replay share of the previous run's mixture". Run A trains with mixture {creative: 1, notebook: 0.5} and a notebook. Run B continues from A with mixture {code: 1}, replay 0.3 and no notebook entries. B is refused before training with `MixtureError: dataset 'notebook' has weight but no usable documents`, although the player gave notebook no weight in B. The replay share inherits A's notebook weight, and the notebook text must be re-sent with every child config. If it is re-sent but has been edited, "replay" trains on the new notebook rather than on what the parent saw. The same applies to coaching.
findings.title: Replay of a parent that trained on a notebook or coaching fails with a MixtureError about a dataset the player did not weight

findings.evidence: Parsed every fixture JSONL: 0 non-ASCII characters in any field. My probe (scratchpad) added accents, emoji, CJK and Greek to the fixtures and ran `airace-content build --scale tiny --fixtures`. findings.evidence: Decoded every id of a tiny-built tok-v1-style tokenizer: 30 ids decode to characters below 0x20 (excluding \n\t\r) or in 0x7f-0x9f. Read cli.py _print_event and _cmd_chat: no sanitising.
findings.fix: Show model text in the CLI with control characters other than \n and \t replaced (e.g. by U+FFFD or a visible escape), as report.cell does. Keep the raw text in telemetry.jsonl.
findings.scenario: With byte-level BPE, every byte is a base token. In tok-v1, about 30 token ids decode to C0/C1 control characters, including ESC (0x1b). An early or garbage-trained model emits them with real probability. `airace-ml train` prints each probe sample and `airace-ml chat` prints each reply verbatim, so ESC sequences reach the owner's Windows Terminal (VT-enabled) and can clear the screen, move the cursor or retitle the window mid-run. report.py already removes these characters (`_CONTROL`, report.py:26), so treatment is inconsistent.
findings.title: CLI prints raw model text, including control characters, while the gate report strips them (spec §11: model output is untrusted wherever it is rendered)

find:tests-health.coverage_note:

I read the core and edge sections of test_infer, test_bench, test_cli, test_gate, test_creativity, content/test_build and test_noise_dedup, and the minipy timing and threading tests. Durations: cold 136.83 s pytest / 3m12s wall (container 4 min after boot); warm 118.15 s / 2m02s wall; 4 vCPUs here.

Skipped and deselected (by design):

findings.evidence: Ran `uv run --no-sync pytest -m "slow or not slow" tests/test_creativity.py::test_build_judge_smoke tests/test_gate.py::test_gate_refuses_to_start_without_its_inputs`: 1 failed, 1 passed. The failure is 'Regex pattern did not match. Expected regex: build-judge. Actual message: the gate cannot start; still to build: the training data under .../data_root0 ...; the novelty index ...'. I confirmed by reading cli.py:679-710 that the bench note lists only the pieces that are missing. The sibling slow test `test_build_judge_resume_smoke` (test_creativity.py:652) already avoids this by copying the root first.
findings.fix: In test_build_judge_smoke, copy tiny_data_root to tmp_path first and build the judge there (`root = tmp_path / 'root'; shutil.copytree(tiny_data_root, root)`), the same way test_build_judge_resume_smoke does. Optionally pass device explicitly too.
findings.scenario: `test_build_judge_smoke` calls `build_judge(tiny_data_root, ...)` on the session-scoped `tiny_data_root` fixture (conftest.py:111), which leaves `judge/v1/calibration.json` and the rest of a judge inside it. Any later test in the same session that relies on the tiny root having no judge then breaks. Running everything with `pytest -m "slow or not slow"` (or `-m ""`) runs test_creativity.py before test_gate.py, and `test_gate_refuses_to_start_without_its_inputs` fails. `test_bench_prints_a_table_and_notes_that_creativity_is_missing` and `test_gate_without_its_inputs_names_what_to_build` in test_cli.py would fail the same way in any order that puts the smoke test first: their output no longer contains 'airace-ml build-judge'. The default suite and `-m slow` on its own both pass.
findings.title: A slow test writes into the shared tiny_data_root, so running slow and default tests together fails test_gate_refuses_to_start_without_its_inputs

findings.evidence: I rebuilt the exact conftest tokenizer (byte-identical) and reproduced sharp_lm. Probe th/bf16_margin.py printed step-0 gap 0.014 vs bf16 max logit error 0.218 for 'Once upon a time'. Probe th/bf16_probe.py, using CPU bf16 autocast as a stand-in for CUDA, found the greedy tokens diverge within 10 steps for 10 of 12 sharp-model seeds; seed 1 happens to agree on CPU. Score sums stayed within the test's rel=0.05 (max 0.021), so only the greedy-equality assertion is fragile.
findings.fix: Compare the paths with a tolerance instead of exact argmax equality. For example, teacher-force the CPU greedy sequence through the GPU model and assert the per-step logits agree within about 0.5 (or that the GPU picks the CPU token whenever the fp32 margin exceeds 1.0). Keep the seeded-sampling reproducibility and probability-range checks.
findings.scenario: `test_cuda_bf16_path_tracks_the_cpu_path` uses `sharp_lm` (seed 1, weights x20, 512-vocab fixture tokenizer) and asserts that 10 greedy tokens on CUDA bf16 autocast equal the CPU fp32 tokens. For 'Once upon a time', the fp32 gap between the top two logits at step 0 is 0.014. bf16 changes the logits by about 0.1-0.6, and steps 3, 5 and ('The cat') 4 also have gaps at or below the bf16 error. The test passed on the owner's RTX 3050 during Tasks 5 and 8, but only because the rounding happened to keep the same argmax. Any edit to tests/fixtures/text/*.txt (which retrains the 512-vocab tokenizer and changes the prompt ids), or a torch or cuBLAS change, re-rolls that luck. Then `pytest -m gpu` fails on the owner's machine even though the CUDA path is fine.
findings.title: The GPU test asserts exact greedy-token equality between CPU fp32 and CUDA bf16, but the fp32 top-2 margin (0.014 logits) is far below bf16 rounding error

findings.evidence: Probe th/tagprobe.py runs `run_benchmarks(ScriptedLM(tok), tok, max_items_per_category=10).tag_breakdown()` and prints `{}`. The MixtureSampler messages for the five brief cases are 'mixture weights must have a positive, finite sum, got sum 0.0', "dataset 'a' has an invalid weight -1.0", and so on. Other tests partly cover both properties: test_bench.py:524-548 checks a non-empty breakdown, and test_sampler.py:174-181 and 205-216 use match=name. The brief tests themselves add nothing.
findings.fix: In test_bench.py:78, use enough items for tags to qualify (e.g. no limit, or 50) and assert the breakdown is non-empty before the range check. In test_sampler.py, give the pools multi-letter names (e.g. 'alpha'/'beta') and assert the offending name with a regex (`match="'beta'"`). For the all-zero case, assert 'sum' explicitly.
findings.scenario: (1) `test_report_serializable_and_tags` asserts `all(0 <= v[0] <= 100 for v in rep.tag_breakdown().values())` with max_items_per_category=10. At 10 items no tag reaches MIN_TAG_ITEMS within a category, so the breakdown is `{}` and the `all()` is trivially true. A breakdown returning NaN or 250 would still pass. (2) `test_invalid_mixtures` checks that the error names the dataset with `any(k in str(e.value) for k in weights)`. For the cases {'a': 0.0} and {'a': -1.0, 'b': 1.0}, the letter 'a' appears in every English message ('...must have a positive...'). A regression that named the wrong dataset, or none, would pass.
findings.title: Two of the brief's tests check nothing: an empty tag breakdown, and dataset names that are single letters

findings.evidence: Decoded every fixture row and counted characters above 127: 0 in all 13 files. Grepped test_build.py, test_corpus.py and test_gate.py: no non-ASCII build input. Non-ASCII appears only in unit tests of textproc and noise functions, and in CLI printing tests. I ran a probe (scratchpad nonascii_build.py) that appends accents, emoji, CJK and a literal <|end|><|ai|> to the tinystories, fineweb, cosmo_stories, simplewiki and soda fixtures and runs build_corpus('tiny'). It completes; the emoji survive decoding in 155/155 creative docs; the literal special strings stay text (end-id count 0 in web, creative and facts). The code works today; only the guard is missing.
findings.fix: Add a few non-ASCII rows to the fixtures (e.g. fineweb, tinystories, soda, gutenberg), or add a test that injects them into a copy of the fixtures. Then assert three things: decoding the corpus docs reproduces the injected strings, known_vocab.txt and simple_vocab.txt round-trip through read_vocab, and the build manifest loads.
findings.scenario: Review Focus 5 requires non-ASCII text (accents, emoji, CJK, curly quotes) to survive the corpus build losslessly and without crashing. Owner: Task 14. All 13 source fixtures contain 0 non-ASCII characters, and test_build.py contains no non-ASCII text. Adapters, noise injection, dedup, quality scoring, the vocab files, tokenizer training, encoding and the manifest therefore never see a non-ASCII byte in any test. The real Hugging Face sources (fineweb, simplewiki, gutenberg, soda) are full of it. A regression on this path would reach the owner's ~137M-token build untested; examples include a normalizer that drops or mangles curly quotes, a non-utf-8 write, or a quality heuristic that zeroes accented text.
findings.title: No test runs non-ASCII text through the corpus build; every source fixture is pure ASCII

findings.evidence: A sys.monitoring line-coverage run of the full default suite (1247 passed) shows 0 executed lines in `_data_identity`, `_growth_sequences`, `_Gate.lm` and `GateRuns._events.on_event`, and gate.py:836-852 unexecuted. Every default test replaces `_load_inputs` (test_gate.py:938). I grepped for identity in the tests: only the constant. Reading the code, `_data_identity` looks correct today (it hashes tags, offsets, info and tokenizer bytes).
findings.fix: Add a default-suite unit test on copies of tiny_data_root. Assert that `_data_identity` is stable across two calls, and that it changes when tags.npz, offsets.npy, the tokenizer, or the token count of one dataset changes. In the fake-gate fixture, also vary `inputs.identity` between runs and assert that everything retrains (25, 15, 15). A small test of `_growth_sequences` ordering (round-robin over DATASET_IDS, at most `length` tokens, skipping docs shorter than 2) would cover G5's inputs.
findings.scenario: Gate run reuse is keyed partly on `_data_identity(root)`, a digest of the tokenizer and each corpus's info, offsets, tags and token-file size. The owner's plan is to rebuild data and rerun the gate into the same --out folder (plan Task 20 step 8: 'Rebuild only what changed, then rerun'). If the identity failed to change after `airace-content build`, about an hour of runs trained on the old corpus would be reused silently, and the G3-G7 verdicts would describe the wrong data. Nothing tests this. The fake gate pins identity to the constant 'data-1' (test_gate.py:932). The reuse test (test_gate.py:1020-1037) varies only the code digests. `_data_identity`, `_growth_sequences`, the successful path of `_load_inputs`, `_Gate.lm`, and GateRuns' progress forwarding (`_events.on_event`, which shows 'step N/M' during gate training) never run in the default suite. Only the two slow gate tests touch them, and those assert reuse, not invalidation.
findings.title: No test checks that the gate's data identity changes when the corpus is rebuilt, and the default suite never runs the gate's real input loading

findings.evidence: Coverage run: trainer.py lines 611 and 618 never execute. grep shows no monkeypatch of rename or PermissionError in test_trainer.py. I wrote probes that pass today. th/finish_resume_probe.py resumes at steps 20, 32 (= _decay_start(40)), 33 and 36 with finishing_mixture={'code':1}; weights and telemetry are identical to the uninterrupted run. th/rollback_resume_probe.py interrupts at the step-30 rollback; the saved snapshot is None, and after resume the weights and telemetry are identical. th/refused_rename_probe.py makes Path.rename raise PermissionError for 'resume'->'resume.old.*' (mode old) and for 'resume.tmp.*'->'resume' (mode tmp); in both modes the resume is identical and leaves no resume.* folders behind.
findings.fix: Add three small default tests from the existing cfg() helper, reusing one module-scoped reference run: resume inside the finishing phase (stop_after_steps >= _decay_start), resume after a rollback at the stop step (loss_override NaN at the stop step), and a monkeypatched Path.rename that raises PermissionError during saves. Each should assert final weights and telemetry equal to the uninterrupted run.
findings.scenario: (1) Line 617-618 re-derives the finishing mixture on resume. This was the fix for the Task 6 deferred minor 'rng_state excludes current weights'. No test resumes a run inside its finishing phase, so a regression (e.g. `>` instead of `>=`, or the line dropped) would silently train the rest of a resumed run on the main mix. (2) Line 611 rebuilds the snapshot when the saved one was None, which happens on an interrupt right after a rollback; no test reaches it. (3) The `contextlib.suppress(OSError)` swap at 599-604 exists for Windows, where a virus scanner or indexer refuses a rename. The docstring promises that training goes on and that resume picks the newest complete state. No test makes a rename fail. The only swap test (test_trainer.py:369-386) simulates crash leftovers. The owner's ~1 h judge build (about 36 saves) runs on Windows.
findings.title: Three resume branches in the trainer, including the Windows 'refused rename' path, are never executed by any test

findings.evidence: `uv run --no-sync pytest --durations=25 -q`: 1247 passed, 1 skipped, 8 deselected in 136.83s (cold); a warm rerun with --durations=0 gave 118.15s. Per-file totals: test_trainer 32.3 s, test_code_instr_grammar 23.5 s, content/test_build 13.4 s, test_bench 10.1 s, test_kb_facts 9.0 s, test_cli 7.9 s. Slowest single tests (warm): test_training_replies_are_right_as_well_as_well_formed 5.4 s, test_spike_rollback_and_stop 3.7 s, test_resume_keeps_the_rollback_snapshot 3.5 s, test_resume_equivalence 3.5 s. Cold outliers: test_train_bench_chat 12.6 s (1.8 s warm) and test_resume_equivalence 7.8 s.
findings.fix: Add a module-scoped fixture that trains the 40-step reference run (and the stop-at-20 partial state, copied per test with shutil.copytree) once. Fold test_resume_equivalence's weight comparison into test_resume_continues_where_it_stopped. That saves about 5-6 s and leaves room for the resume tests proposed above. Keep tracking the suite time in the ledger as each milestone adds tests.
findings.scenario: The default suite took 136.8 s by pytest's clock on a cold container (3m12s wall including uv and torch cold start) and 118.2 s warm (2m02s wall), on 4 vCPUs. It is under the 3-minute budget, but the margin will be thinner on Windows, where Defender scans the many tmp corpora and checkpoints the suite writes. That machine's first run after boot will also be cold. test_trainer.py is the largest file at 32.3 s (27%). test_resume_equivalence, test_resume_continues_where_it_stopped and test_resume_recovers_from_an_interrupted_swap each train the identical 40-step `cfg(token_budget=1024*40)` reference run and the same stop-at-20 partial run. The first two are nearly the same test: both run full + stop-at-20 with checkpoint_every=10 + resume, and one compares weights while the other compares telemetry.
findings.title: The default suite is at 118-137 s on this machine; trainer tests repeat the same reference training runs

findings.evidence: Read build.py:285-418, manifest.py and both CLIs. Ran probe_tiny_then_full.py (scratchpad): build_corpus('tiny') trained tokenizer 3c06b03e6f9b. A following build_corpus('full', same root), with assembly stubbed to stand in for the network, returned tokenizer_trained=False and the same tokenizer hash 3c06b03e6f9b. The tiny-trained tokenizer also reaches the full 4096 entries (checked), so even a vocab-size check on reuse would not catch it.
findings.fix: Record the tokenizer's provenance when it is trained, e.g. a sidecar or manifest field with the scale and the sample bytes. At --scale full, refuse with a BuildError (exit 1, saying to add --retrain-tokenizer or use another --out) to reuse a tokenizer or shared artifacts (simple_vocab, known_vocab, false_facts) that were made at a different scale. Apply the VOCAB_SIZE check to a reused tokenizer at full scale too. Alternatively, retrain automatically when every dataset is built and the existing tokenizer came from a tiny build.
findings.scenario: The local session or the owner does the 'quick test set' build first. The airace-ml CLI suggests exactly that (cli.py:94: 'airace-content build --scale tiny (a quick test set) or --scale full'), and CLAUDE.md lists both scales. That tiny build writes data/tokenizer/tok-v1/tokenizer.json, trained on about 1,200 short documents. Next comes the real 'airace-content build --scale full' (hours of Hugging Face streaming). At build.py:311, train_tok = retrain_tokenizer or not tok_path.exists() is False, so all 137M tokens are encoded with the tiny tokenizer. The only sign is the line 'tokenizer: frozen, reused' (content cli.py:94). The vocab-size assert that Task 2 deferred to Task 14/15 (build.py:387) only checks a newly trained tokenizer, never a reused one. Nothing records which scale trained the tokenizer (manifest.py:48-70). The novelty index, the judge (about 1 h of GPU), every gate run and every future player model then sit on this weak 'frozen' tok-v1. A partial full-scale build after a tiny build is worse: reusable() (build.py:324-326) also reuses the tiny simple_vocab.txt (built from 5,000 rows instead of 200,000) and the tiny known_vocab.txt, so real web text gets quality scores against a tiny vocabulary and Thorough cleaning drops most of it.
findings.title: A full corpus build silently reuses a tokenizer left by an earlier tiny build in the same data root, and freezes it as tok-v1

findings.evidence: Ran probe_judge_reuse.py (scratchpad). Tiny build seed 0 (tokenizer 3c06b03e6f9b), shrunk judge built (7 training events). Rebuilt with seed 1 and --retrain-tokenizer (tokenizer 310c5f02da56). build_judge again emitted 0 training events, data/judge/v1/tokenizer.json became 310c5f02da56 while the weights were still the 3c06 model, and calibration.json was rewritten (p90 7.75 -> 8.19) with no error. Read judge.py, novelty.py and gate.py _load_judge/_load_novelty/_check_* to confirm no provenance check exists.
findings.fix: When the judge's training completes, store a digest of the training data (the gate's _data_identity, or at least the tokenizer's sha256) in train_config.json, and make _trained() require it to match, so build-judge retrains after a rebuild. Store the same digest in the novelty index .json. In _load_judge/_load_novelty (gate) and _creativity_tools (cli bench), compare it with the data root and raise the existing 'out of date ... Rebuild it with: …' error on a mismatch.
findings.scenario: The corpus is rebuilt after the judge exists, for example with --retrain-tokenizer after spotting the problem in finding 1, or a full rebuild after Task 15's license or recipe fixes. The local session then runs 'airace-ml build-judge' again, as CLAUDE.md's order suggests. _trained() (judge.py:235-243) compares only the recipe config, so the judge is not retrained. build_judge copies the NEW tokenizer into data/judge/v1 (judge.py:293) next to a model trained on the OLD token ids, recalibrates it and reports success. Judge.load only checks the vocab size (judge.py:102-106), which is 4096 for both. From then on every creativity score and the gate's G2 well-formed check use a judge that reads text through the wrong id mapping, and its calibration percentiles adapt to the garbage, so nothing looks broken. The novelty index has the same gap: its .json records only hash_base, n, sample_mod and count (gate.py:789-795, novelty.py:197-209), never which corpus or tokenizer it indexes. A stale index after a re-tokenize makes almost every window 'new', which inflates creativity. The gate's own runs are keyed by _data_identity (gate.py:721-735), but its judge and index are not checked against it. The only mitigation ('delete data/judge/v1 before build-judge') is written in the SDD ledger alone, not in CLAUDE.md, the build-judge help or the handoff README.
findings.title: build-judge and the gate silently use a judge and a novelty index built from older corpora or another tokenizer (Task 17 deferred minor, still present)

findings.evidence: Ran the deferred Task 16 real-tokenizer test with AIRACE_DATA pointing at a tiny fixture build's 4096-entry tokenizer. It failed with [('knowledge-0168', 'Bandar Seri Begawan', 9, 8), ('knowledge-0168', ' Bandar Seri Begawan', 9, 8)]. 'Santo Domingo' (knowledge-0155) took 7 of 8. Measured 13.8 'Begawan' per MB in fact_prose_docs output (probe_begawan.py).
findings.fix: Before bench-v1 is first measured, give exact items headroom: a default of about 12, or a per-item budget derived from the longest accepted answer (for example len(answer)//2 + 4). Extraction already cuts at the first comma or newline, so the extra tokens cost little.
findings.line: 116 (ExactItem.max_new_tokens = 8); answer from skills/kb_data/countries.json:88; check in tests/test_bench.py:737-739
findings.scenario: Every ExactItem gets 8 new tokens. Under a 4096-entry byte-level BPE trained on a tiny build, ' Bandar Seri Begawan' encodes to 9 tokens. 'Begawan' occurs only about 14 times per MB of generated fact prose, so the real 20 MB tokenizer sample is unlikely to merge it much either. If tok-v1 also needs 9 or more tokens, generation stops at 8 tokens before the answer is complete, so knowledge-0168 cannot be answered by any model. On the owner's machine, test_every_answer_fits_its_reply_budget_with_the_real_tokenizer starts running once data/tokenizer exists and would fail right after Task 15. The item would have to be fixed after bench-v1 has been measured, which is the point where the bench freezes.
findings.title: bench-v1 knowledge item knowledge-0168 ('Bandar Seri Begawan') may not fit its 8-token reply budget under the real tok-v1
